corrections.new: Right common carotid artery (from the brachiocephalic trunk behind the right sternoclavicular joint); left common carotid artery (directly from the aortic arch, so it has a thoracic part). Each ends at the carotid bifurcation as the internal carotid artery (to brain and orbit) and external carotid artery (to face, scalp and neck).
corrections.reason: Right/left origins and terminal division were not set out as divisions; model has separate right and left meshes.

corrections.new: Cervical part (bifurcation to carotid canal; no branches). Petrous part (in the carotid canal of the temporal bone; caroticotympanic artery, artery of pterygoid canal). Cavernous part (in the cavernous sinus; meningohypophyseal trunk with tentorial, dorsal meningeal and inferior hypophyseal branches, artery to inferior cavernous sinus/inferolateral trunk, recurrent artery of foramen lacerum, branches to foramen rotundum, ovale and spinosum, meningeal and cavernous branches). Cerebral part (above the anterior clinoid; ophthalmic, superior hypophyseal, posterior communicating and anterior choroidal arteries, ending as anterior and middle cerebral arteries).
corrections.reason: Netter names the four parts and the foraminal/lacerum branches, which the card lacked as a Divisions entry.

corrections.new: Mandibular (1st) part, behind the neck of the mandible: deep auricular, anterior tympanic, middle meningeal, accessory meningeal, inferior alveolar (with mylohyoid branch). Pterygoid (2nd) part, on or deep to lateral pterygoid: anterior and posterior deep temporal, masseteric, medial and lateral pterygoid, buccal. Pterygopalatine (3rd) part, in the pterygopalatine fossa: posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital (with middle and anterior superior alveolar), descending palatine (greater and lesser palatine), artery of pterygoid canal, pharyngeal, sphenopalatine (posterior lateral nasal and posterior septal branches).
corrections.reason: The three parts were only described under Course; Netter shows the branches of each part.

corrections.new: Frontal (anterior) branch: runs forward over the temple to the forehead, anastomoses with supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries. Parietal (posterior) branch: runs up and back over the parietal scalp, anastomoses with posterior auricular and occipital arteries. Collateral branches before the division: transverse facial, middle temporal, zygomatico-orbital and anterior auricular arteries.
corrections.reason: Terminal frontal and parietal branches labelled by Netter were not marked as divisions.

corrections.new: Frontal (anterior) branch: crosses the greater wing of the sphenoid deep to the pterion, supplies anterior dura and calvaria. Parietal (posterior) branch: curves back over the squamous temporal and parietal bone, supplies posterior dura and calvaria.
corrections.reason: Netter labels the frontal (anterior) and parietal (posterior) branches; now marked as divisions.

corrections.new: Posterior lateral nasal branches (to the conchae, meatuses and sinuses of the lateral wall); posterior septal branches (across the sphenoid face to the septum, anastomosing with the greater palatine artery in the incisive canal).
corrections.reason: Two terminal groups labelled by Netter and present as separate model meshes.

corrections.new: Right subclavian (from the brachiocephalic trunk) and left subclavian (from the aortic arch). Each has three parts by its relation to the anterior scalene. 1st part (medial to the muscle): vertebral artery, internal thoracic artery, thyrocervical trunk. 2nd part (behind the muscle): costocervical trunk. 3rd part (lateral to the muscle, to the outer border of the 1st rib): dorsal scapular artery when it does not arise from the transverse cervical.
corrections.reason: Parts relative to anterior scalene and right/left origins set out as divisions; Netter labels right subclavian and each branch.

corrections.new: Prevertebral part (V1): subclavian to the transverse foramen of C6. Cervical part (V2): through the transverse foramina of C6 to C1; segmental medullary and muscular branches. Atlantic part (V3, horizontal segment): in the groove on the posterior arch of the atlas within the suboccipital triangle. Intracranial part (V4): through the foramen magnum; anterior and posterior meningeal branches, posterior spinal, posterior inferior cerebellar and anterior spinal arteries, then joins its fellow as the basilar.
corrections.ref: Plate 147 (p. 202); Plate 154 (p. 209); back section, suboccipital triangle plate
corrections.reason: Netter labels the cervical part, the horizontal segment and the intracranial part; the card used only V1 to V4.

corrections.new: Superficial branch (superficial cervical artery): deep to trapezius with the accessory nerve. Deep branch (dorsal scapular artery): deep to levator scapulae and the rhomboids along the medial border of the scapula; arises with the superficial branch in about 30%, otherwise directly from the subclavian.
corrections.reason: Netter labels superficial and deep branches and the 30% common origin.

corrections.new: A1 (precommunicating) segment: internal carotid to anterior communicating artery; anteromedial central arteries. A2 (postcommunicating) segment: in the longitudinal fissure; long medial striate artery (recurrent artery of Heubner), medial frontobasal (orbitofrontal) artery, frontopolar artery. Terminal trunks: callosomarginal artery (anterior, intermediate and posterior medial frontal branches, cingular branches, paracentral artery) and pericallosal artery (precuneal artery, terminal branches to the medial parietal lobe).
corrections.reason: Segments and cortical branches gathered as divisions; cingular branches were absent from the card.

corrections.new: M1 (sphenoidal) segment: anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) arteries. M2 (insular) segment: superior and inferior trunks over the insula. M3 (opercular) and M4 (cortical) segments, giving in order: lateral frontobasal (orbitofrontal) artery, prefrontal artery, artery of precentral sulcus, artery of central sulcus, artery of postcentral sulcus (anterior parietal), posterior parietal artery, artery to angular gyrus, and anterior, middle and posterior temporal branches (with the polar temporal artery).
corrections.reason: Netter labels the M1 segment and each cortical branch; M2 to M4 are standard segment names not labelled by Netter.

corrections.new: P1 (precommunicating) segment: basilar bifurcation to the posterior communicating artery; thalamoperforating (posteromedial central) arteries. P2 (postcommunicating) segment: around the cerebral crus; thalamogeniculate arteries, posterior medial and posterior lateral choroidal arteries. Cortical branches: anterior and posterior temporal and occipitotemporal branches (lateral occipital artery), and the medial occipital artery giving the dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal), parieto-occipital branch and calcarine branch.
corrections.reason: P1/P2 segments and cortical branches set out as divisions; medial occipital artery and occipitotemporal branches were absent.

notes: Divisions added to cards with true parts, segments or terminal divisions even where the same facts were scattered under Course/Branches, so the divisions are marked under one label; pure branch lists already complete under Branches (external carotid, facial, lingual, occipital, thyrocervical and costocervical trunks, ophthalmic, basilar, PICA, etc.) were left unchanged. Netter labels only: ICA cervical/petrous/cavernous/cerebral parts; vertebral cervical part, horizontal segment and intracranial part; A1/A2, M1, P1/P2. The names of the three maxillary parts, the subclavian parts, vertebral prevertebral/atlantic (V1-V4) and M2-M4 are standard terms not printed in Netter (marked netter-inferred). Model mapping fixes: 'Anterior temporal branch' and 'Posterior temporal branch' were attached to superficial-temporal-artery, but their bounding boxes lie inside the skull at the level of the MCA temporal branches (x<=0.069 vs parietal bone 0.074), so they are MCA temporal branches; 'Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery' is the accessory meningeal artery, which already has a card. 'Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk' is not a head-and-neck artery and Netter's H&N section does not label it: left unmapped. 'Parietal branches of middle cerebral artery' and the M1/M2/M3 segment meshes stay on middle-cerebral-artery. Group cards (deep temporal/masseteric/buccal, labial, ciliary, supraorbital/supratrochlear, spinal) were not split to avoid duplicates.
